page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 31.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at 2.3 GHz, this instance allocates 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. It includes a substantial 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, alongside advanced CPU instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and INT8 operations. The instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Performance benchmarks reveal a strong single-core profile, with Geekbench single-core and text processing scores reaching top-tier levels. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also demonstrate strong performance. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are generally weaker, with stress-ng multi-core, Passmark CPU, and uncached memory read/write speeds falling into lower performance tiers. Static web serving throughput and LLM inference speeds for small and medium models remain in the average range.

From a resource density perspective, the c4-highmem-4 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 7.75 GB per core, providing qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. The lack of local storage and bundled GPUs represents a clear tradeoff, positioning this instance for workloads such as memory-bound databases, text processing, single-threaded data manipulation, and lightweight web serving.
